title: A conserved monocyte activation program links brain injury to systemic immune adaptation and clinical outcomes.
authors: Sadek, Abderrahmane; Petrier, Melanie; Fourgeux, Cynthia; Braud, Martin; Gourain, Victor; Bouras, Marwan; Poulain, Cecile; Moumni, Mohieddine; Roquilly, Antoine; Poschmann, Jeremie
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脑损伤后单核细胞转录程序与临床结局，虽涉及转录因子PU.1，但核心为免疫转录组与代谢建模，无蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: RATIONALE: Systemic immune dysregulation after traumatic brain injury (TBI) contributes to secondary complications and influences long-term recovery, yet the cellular and molecular dynamics remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: To characterize longitudinal immune responses following TBI and identify conserved transcriptional programs linked to clinical outcomes and mechanistically regulated monocyte states with potential prognostic and therapeutic significance. METHODS: We conducted longitudinal transcriptomic profiling of PBMCs from TBI patients (n =65 samples) at Day 1, Day 7, and Month 6 post-injury, alongside healthy controls (n =24). Cell type composition was assessed using computational deconvolution and validated by flow cytometry. Gene co-expression networks were constructed to identify temporally dynamic immune signatures. Monocyte-specific metabolic activity was inferred using genome-scale metabolic modeling and confirmed by plasma metabolite quantification. Genome-wide chromatin state was assessed by H3K27ac ChIP-sequencing in CD14(+) monocytes. External validation was performed across independent PBMC and monocyte datasets from bacterial and viral infections, including COVID-19 and pneumonia. MAIN RESULTS: TBI patients showed a transient increase in circulating monocytes at Day 1 and Day 7, returning to baseline by Month 6. Weighted gene co-expression analysis identified a data-driven monocyte-associated co-expression module (Yellow module) that dominated early responses and tracked with monocyte abundance. This module was conserved in sorted CD14(+) monocytes from an independent cohort and reflected sustained inflammatory activation. Metabolomic and flux balance analyses revealed coordinated remodeling of the aspartate-arginine-ornithine axis, indicating nitrogen stress and altered metabolic demands during monocyte activation. In external datasets of PBMCs from patients with acute infections, Yellow module expression was associated with clinical severity and independently predicted survival. Epigenomic profiling revealed dynamic enhancer remodeling at Yellow module loci, with PU.1 (SPI1), a monocyte lineage-defining transcription factor, identified as a putative upstream regulator linking transcriptional activation to regulatory architecture. CONCLUSIONS: TBI induces a prognostically informative, monocyte-enriched transcriptional program marked by inflammatory and metabolic reprogramming. This epigenetically regulated state is conserved across critical illness, correlates with patient outcomes, and identifies PU.1 as a key regulator of monocyte activation. These findings support the Yellow module as a candidate biomarker for risk stratification and a mechanistic link between brain injury and systemic immune adaptation.
abstract_zh: RATIONALE：创伤性脑损伤（TBI）后的系统性免疫失调导致继发性并发症并影响长期恢复，但其细胞和分子动态仍未被完全理解。OBJECTIVES：旨在表征TBI后的纵向免疫反应，并识别与临床结果相关的保守转录程序，以及具有潜在预后和治疗意义的机制性调控单核细胞状态。METHODS：我们对TBI患者（n =65个样本）在损伤后第1天、第7天和第6个月，以及健康对照组（n =24）进行了PBMCs的纵向转录组学分析。使用计算去卷积评估细胞类型组成，并通过流式细胞术验证。构建基因共表达网络以识别时间动态免疫特征。使用基因组规模代谢模型推断单核细胞特异性代谢活性，并通过血浆代谢物定量确认。通过CD14(+)单核细胞中的H3K27ac ChIP-测序评估全基因组染色质状态。在来自细菌和病毒感染（包括COVID-19和肺炎）的独立PBMC和单核细胞数据集中进行外部验证。MAIN RESULTS：TBI患者在第1天和第7天显示循环单核细胞短暂增加，在第6个月恢复到基线。加权基因共表达分析识别出一个数据驱动的单核细胞相关共表达模块（Yellow模块），该模块主导早期反应并追踪单核细胞丰度。该模块在独立队列的分选CD14(+)单核细胞中保守，并反映持续炎症激活。代谢组学和通量平衡分析揭示了天冬氨酸-精氨酸-鸟氨酸轴的协调重塑，表明单核细胞激活期间的氮应激和代谢需求改变。在急性感染患者PBMCs的外部数据集中，Yellow模块表达与临床严重程度相关，并独立预测生存。表观基因组分析揭示了Yellow模块位点的动态增强子重塑，其中PU.1（SPI1），一种单核细胞谱系定义转录因子，被识别为将转录激活与调控架构联系起来的假定上游调节因子。CONCLUSIONS：TBI诱导一个具有预后信息价值的、单核细胞富集的转录程序，其特征为炎症和代谢重编程。这种表观遗传调控状态在危重疾病中保守，与患者结果相关，并识别PU.1为单核细胞激活的关键调节因子。这些发现支持Yellow模块作为风险分层的候选生物标志物，以及脑损伤与系统性免疫适应之间的机制联系。
